title: Learning goals
text: Compute a weighted cut edge by edge · Check complete, disjoint assignments · Distinguish counts from areas
transcript:
Compute a weighted cut edge by edge
Check complete, disjoint assignments
Distinguish counts from areas
Interpret ratio and imbalance
Recognize an infeasible low cut
Write testable metric functions

title: 01 · Check the assignment first
text: Represent circuit cells by vertices and connections by undirected edges. An edge weight models the cost of placing its endpoints in different regions. This is a deliberately simple model: it does not
transcript: Represent circuit cells by vertices and connections by undirected edges. An edge weight models the cost of placing its endpoints in different regions. This is a deliberately simple model: it does not predict complete routed wire length or timing. It does let us compare assignments under a clearly defined objective.

title: 02 · Count each crossing edge once
text: The objective is cut = Σ w(u,v)·[part(u) ≠ part(v)]. The bracket is 1 when its condition is true and 0 otherwise. Endpoint labels determine whether an edge crosses. Its position on the
transcript: The objective is cut = Σ w(u,v)·[part(u) ≠ part(v)]. The bracket is 1 when its condition is true and 0 otherwise. Endpoint labels determine whether an edge crosses. Its position on the screen, or an intersection with another drawn line, has no effect.

title: 03 · Counts, areas and capacities
text: When every size equals 1, counts and areas coincide. Change A's size to 4: ABC still contains three vertices, but its area becomes 6; DE has count and area 2. Under capacity
transcript: When every size equals 1, counts and areas coincide. Change A's size to 4: ABC still contains three vertices, but its area becomes 6; DE has count and area 2. Under capacity 4, ABC | DE has a low cut of 3 but is infeasible.

title: 04 · Two balance summaries
text: For side areas s0 and s1, ratio = min(s0,s1)/max(s0,s1), where values closer to 1 are more even. Imbalance = |s0−s1|/(s0+s1), where values closer to 0 are more even. For areas 2 and
transcript: For side areas s0 and s1, ratio = min(s0,s1)/max(s0,s1), where values closer to 1 are more even. Imbalance = |s0−s1|/(s0+s1), where values closer to 0 are more even. For areas 2 and 3 the values are 2/3 and 1/5. Their thresholds are not interchangeable.

title: 05 · Feasibility precedes optimization
text: An optimization problem has an objective and constraints. Here the objective minimizes cut; constraints require a complete, disjoint, nonempty assignment and the declared balance or capacity. Filter for legality before comparing costs.
transcript: An optimization problem has an objective and constraints. Here the objective minimizes cut; constraints require a complete, disjoint, nonempty assignment and the declared balance or capacity. Filter for legality before comparing costs. Mixing illegal and legal assignments rewards avoiding the problem's rules.

title: 06 · Implement a reliable evaluator
text: Validate unique vertex names, positive sizes, existing endpoints and finite weights. Then verify that the assignment supplies a valid part for every vertex. An adjacency list often stores each undirected edge twice.
transcript: Validate unique vertex names, positive sizes, existing endpoints and finite weights. Then verify that the assignment supplies a valid part for every vertex. An adjacency list often stores each undirected edge twice. Summing it directly double-counts; the normalized edge list used here stores each edge once.

title: Check the common mistakes
text: A low cut is always good
transcript: All on one side has cut 0 but can violate nonempty or capacity constraints. Check legality first.
